Before 2009, every point of lost capacity cost between a third of a point and a full point of unemployment, and the level rarely fell back to where it had been.

The 1966/67 recession, mild by later standards, helped bring down Ludwig Erhard's government and tripled registered unemployment; by June 1967 the new grand coalition had passed the Stability and Growth Act.
The 1992/93 downturn fed a rise that peaked at 12.7 percent in 1997 and was answered, a decade later, by the Hartz reforms.
2009 broke the pattern.
